title: Maximum Path Sum in a Binary Tree
statement: A binary tree is given as `tree`, a non-empty list in level-order (breadth-first) array form: tree[0] is the root, and the tree is built level by level by reading the array left to right. For each non-null node consumed, its next two not-yet-assigned child slots (in the order they appear) become its left and right child; missing children are written as null. Node values may be negative. A downward-connected path is any sequence of one or more nodes where each successive node is a child of the previous one, but the path may also fork through a single node so that it descends into the left subtree, passes through that node once, and continues down into the right subtree (i.e. the path is a simple path in the tree that never moves from a node up to its parent more than to reach a shared topmost node). Concretely, for each node the candidate path sum is the node's value plus the best downward extension into its left subtree (or 0 if that would be negative) plus the best downward extension into its right subtree (or 0 if that would be negative). Return the maximum such sum over all nodes. A single node by itself is a valid path, so the answer is at least the largest single node value. Since `tree` is non-empty, an answer always exists; return the integer sum.
hints: Each node asks the same recursive question: what is the best path that bends through me, and separately, what is the best straight branch I can hand upward to my parent?

Do a post-order DFS. From a child, only accept its contribution if it is positive (clamp with max(0, dfs(child))); update a running best with node.val + left + right, but return only node.val + max(left, right) to the parent so a forked path is never extended further.

Keep the global answer in a mutable holder initialized to the root value. At each node compute left = max(0, dfs(left)) and right = max(0, dfs(right)); set best = max(best, node.val + left + right) (the through-node path), then return node.val + max(left, right) (the single extendable branch). The final answer is the holder after visiting the root.
